QF.id: Clubbing, Set-Off and Carry Forward of Losses_20

question.text: The term "substantial interest" for the purpose of clubbing of income under Section 64(1)(ii) means holding beneficial ownership of at least what percentage of voting power or profit share in a concern?

explanation.text: The Logic: For the clubbing provisions of the Income-tax Act dealing with remuneration paid by a concern in which an individual has a "substantial interest", substantial interest is generally defined as holding at least 20% of the voting power in a company, or being entitled to at least 20% of the profits in a non-corporate concern such as a partnership firm, at any time during the previous year. Beneficial ownership at this level brings the related-spouse remuneration within the clubbing rule (subject to the professional-qualification exception). The Trap: 10% is a threshold used in some other tax provisions but is below the clubbing-rule threshold. 26% is associated with special-resolution blocking rights under company-law contexts and not with the clubbing definition of substantial interest. 51% corresponds to majority control, which is not the threshold used by the clubbing rule. Note: The cited workbook chapter discusses general clubbing of income, spouse/son's-wife categories, and gift/relative rules, but does not explicitly state the 20% substantial-interest threshold for Section 64(1)(ii). The framing above reflects general Income-tax Act knowledge of the clubbing-rule definition of substantial interest rather than a direct workbook citation.
